GHSA-47qp-hqvx-6r3f is a heap-exhaustion DoS in JLine's remote-telnet server: TelnetIO.readNEVariables() accumulates Telnet NEW-ENVIRON variable pairs into an unbounded HashMap with no per-connection cap, allowing an OutOfMemoryError. Data Prepper does not run a JLine telnet server. The upstream build pins org.jline:jline to 3.25.0 via a build.gradle dependency constraint ('because CVE-2023-50572'), purely as a transitive terminal/line-reader library; Data Prepper's own source references org.jline:jline-remote-telnet and the org.jline.builtins.telnet API in zero places (verified by code search across opensearch-project/data-prepper at tag 2.15.1). No source, sink, or processor plugin instantiates the Telnet server, the default shipped pipeline is random -> stdout, and the management server is com.sun.net.httpserver on port 4900 with http_basic auth. The vulnerable Telnet server code is never on an execute path in this image.

The vulnerable Telnet server code is never on an execute path in this image.

The vulnerability is in the JLine3 Telnet server (remote-telnet module) which allows unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion via unbounded Telnet NEW-ENVIRON variables. Druid does not instantiate or expose a JLine Telnet server; jline is bundled as a transitive dependency (via the org.jline:jline uber-jar) for CLI line-reading only. The telnet server code is present in the uber-jar but is never loaded or executed in Druid's runtime. The fix exists only in jline 4.x (all 3.x versions are affected) and upgrading is a major version change incompatible with the current dependency tree.
